notes: Verified: `go build ./...` OK, `go test ./internal/proxy/` (full package, 56s) passes; the five new tests would fail on main (they call new routes/functions and assert 200 on metadata and tools/list with a real RS256 token signed against a fake JWKS; refusals assert message substrings and the WWW-Authenticate challenge).

Auth path change is additive and gated: internal/proxy/server.go:1587 only enters the SSO branch when path ∈ {/mcp,/mcp/gateway} AND bearer is JWT-shaped AND mcp.oauth.enabled+issuer set; the proxy-key path (lines 1543-1581) is untouched and tested (TestAProxyKeyStillWorksWhenMCPSSOIsOn). With the feature on and auth disabled, a JWT-shaped bearer on the MCP paths is no longer passed through as an external upstream key — intentional and stated in the code comment, but it is a behavior change for that (unusual) configuration.

Account resolution falls back to the token's `email` claim (mcp_oauth.go:312) without checking `email_verified`; this mirrors the existing web sign-in merge rule (keycloak_handlers.go:235) so it is parity, not a new hole, but it means a realm that allows unverified self-registration could map a token onto a pre-existing local account with the same email (scopes still capped to mcp.oauth.scopes ∩ role).

Issuer normalization mismatch: mcp_oauth.go:71 trims a trailing '/' from IssuerURL before AuthIdentityBySubject, while the web sign-in stores identities with the untrimmed kc.IssuerURL (keycloak_handlers.go:264). If the admin configured the issuer with a trailing slash the subject lookup misses and only the email fallback works; accounts whose email is the `sub@sso.local` placeholder would be refused as unregistered.

mcp.oauth.scopes validator accepts an empty string; an empty value makes scopes_supported encode as JSON null and every SSO principal end up with zero scopes (scope_denied on /mcp). The UI save path substitutes 'mcp:use' but the by-key API does not.

mcpOAuthSettings.active() logs a Warn on every evaluation when enabled but the issuer is empty — this runs on every MCP 401 (writeMCPUnauthorized) and on every JWT-shaped bearer, so a misconfigured deployment gets one warn line per refused request.

Metadata under /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp/gateway advertises resource=…/mcp (the parent), relying on clients accepting a prefix resource (MCP TS/Python SDKs do). If an admin sets mcp.oauth.resource to the /mcp/gateway URL itself, /mcp tokens would need aud=…/mcp/gateway exactly; documented resource examples use /mcp so this is only a configuration footgun.
rememberMCPOAuthRefusal mutates *http.Request in place (`*r = *r.WithContext(...)`) to hand the refusal to the handler; works because the handler owns the pointer, but it is an unusual pattern.
No migrations, no external state, all settings default off; revert is a clean code revert. Scope is on-target (feature code, tests, admin card, docs); no unrelated refactors or dependency changes.
